pr_title: Added new connection plugin prepare_command method
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
Adds a new method to the connection plugins that allow plugins to control how a command is processed before being run. This API provides the extra information needed as discrete objects rather than an already processed command string.

Fixes the psrp connection to support script setting chdir by using this new API.

Fixes: https://github.com/ansible/ansible/issues/81277

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bugfix Pull Request
- Feature Pull Request

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
The `allow_executable` shell attribute overrides have been removed as the logic is consolidated into one area. The attribute is still checked to allow backwards compatibility with connection plugins outside of Ansible. Sometime in the future this attribute should potentially be deprecated to simplify the plugins a bit more.

review_comments: I'm still not too happy with how this part turned out. The `sleep 0` code should only be set in ssh but for ssh to only do this it would need to reimplement this whole method. Will need to think about this one a bit more which allows a connection plugin to customise this specific bit of code while keeping the cmd + become stuff before this.

Not just ssh, local and paramiko too (probably most non windows ones) , this was mostly added for OSs that have a 'immediate success' on fork/run subshell command, but really did not work if you closed the connection right away (solaris ...).

The code specifically singles out ssh here, even the commit that added it talks about it being a problem for ssh/paramiko https://github.com/ansible/ansible/commit/bad293ae3537a9d951636b571c8b74df6d8a12b0. I wonder if @mattclay remembers the details around this.

The `sleep 0` was added specifically to address a Linux kernel bug that affected `sshd` from OpenSSH, see: https://github.com/ansible/ansible/issues/13876#issuecomment-250776339

Since the kernel bug has been fixed for quite a while now, we should consider making this work-around opt-in through config.
it also affects solaris due to how they implemented fork

I was hoping to avoid adding this attribute but a connection cannot use `self._play_context.get_loader().get_basedir()` as the play context does have the `get_loader()` method but it is no longer set. This is just how it was set before for the `local` connection plugin.
